sections.html:
Start with permit records. The city building department regulates a long list of home work, and buyers want proof it was done right. St. Cloud is in Osceola County on the shore of East Lake Tohopekaliga, and buyers weigh that lake setting along with the distance to Kissimmee and the rest of the county.

A quick sale goes best when three things are ready: the deed, the permits for any roof, window, pool or air conditioning work, and a clear idea of the tax bill. Gather them before you talk to any buyer, whether that is an agent, a private buyer or a company offering cash.

sections.h2: Permits the City of St. Cloud requires
sections.html:
A permit is often required before a project starts, and the building department works under the 8th Edition of the Florida Building Code. The city sets the ultimate design wind speed at 140 MPH for Risk Category II buildings.

Permit or no permit: sample projects in St. Cloud
Permit requiredNo permit needed
ReroofPainting
Window and door replacementCarpeting and cabinets
Swimming pool and spaGutters
Solar photovoltaicReplacing a faucet with the existing supply and drain
Accessory dwelling unit, shed, carportReplacing a water closet in the existing location
Siding or soffit over 25% of the structureInterior door replacement

Demolition, docks, hurricane shutters, screen enclosures and electrical service upgrades are permitted work too. The city does not take cash at its counters, permit fees included.

sections.h2: Wind rules and what buyers ask
sections.html:
With a 140 MPH design wind speed, roofs, window and door units, shutters and screen enclosures are inspected against a wind standard, and replacing them takes a permit. Buyers, insurers and inspectors ask about those items first.

If your roof or windows were replaced, find the permit number and final inspection. If hurricane shutters went in, the city lists them as permitted work as well. A ready file shows that the biggest wind-related parts were done properly, which backs your price and shortens negotiation.

If emergency repairs had to be made fast, the permit application is due by the next working business day, so check that a late permit did not slip through.

sections.h2: Repairs that matter before a sale
sections.html:
Open permits tend to hide behind structural, mechanical and electrical work. When an earlier owner or a contractor did the job, call the building department and ask if the permit reached final inspection.

  • Roof, window and door replacements.
  • Pool, spa and screen enclosure work.
  • Additions, sheds, garages and accessory dwelling units.
  • Solar installations and electrical service upgrades.

The city links to Florida's lien law and to guidance on the dangers of owner-builder permits. Pulled an owner-builder permit yourself? The department can explain how to close it out. Closing gaps invites more kinds of buyers, but a cash buyer may be fine with the house unchanged.

sections.h2: Sheds, accessory units and manufactured homes
sections.html:
Accessory dwelling units, sheds, gazebos, carports, garages, docks, flagpoles and manufactured or modular structures all count as regulated work. A backyard structure that was never permitted is a common surprise in a buyer's review.

If you have one, ask the building department how it was classified and what a retroactive permit would take. Siding or soffit work over 25 percent of a structure needs a permit, while smaller repairs to wood siding and stucco over block do not. Cash buyers can often accept an unpermitted shed or carport, but it may shape their price.

sections.h2: Osceola County property taxes at a sale
sections.html:
In Osceola County, the appraiser fixes each parcel's value as of January 1 and the tax collector mails the bills in November. A capped Save Our Homes assessment is lifted to just value after a sale, which can leave the new owner with a larger bill than yours.

Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Apply to the appraiser by March 1, and make sure the house was your permanent residence on January 1. Anyone who pays early gets a printed discount that steps down from 4 percent in November to 3, then 2, then 1 percent in February.

The August mailing is the notice of proposed taxes. Your closing agent prorates that year's bill between you and the buyer, and the appraiser can tell you which exemptions are on your parcel.

sections.h2: Stamp tax and recording on a St. Cloud deed
sections.html:
Each deed here is taxed by the state at 70 cents for every $100 of consideration, collected by the Osceola County clerk when the deed is filed. Under Department of Revenue rules every party to the document is liable, no matter who the contract says will pay.

Section 28.24 sets the clerk's page fees at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, along with smaller per-page charges. Expect your title agent to list them line by line.

Before accepting a cash offer, ask who pays stamp tax, title insurance and recording, and how many days the buyer needs.

sections.h2: Which offices handle a St. Cloud sale?
sections.html:
Three county offices touch the sale. The property appraiser sets just value every January 1, mails the August notice and decides who qualifies for exemptions. The tax collector issues the November bill, accepts payment, and takes deferral and installment requests. The clerk of the circuit court files your deed and takes the stamp tax.

  • Disagree with your value? You have 25 days from the August notice to petition the clerk.
  • A denied exemption or classification goes to the value adjustment board, and the petition is due 30 days after the denial letter is mailed.
  • Ask the tax collector for a payoff of any balance ahead of closing, so the closing agent can clear it.

These deadlines come around every year, so an appeal made after a sale covers only the tax year still open. Keep the August notice and the exemption papers in your sale folder, because a buyer or title agent may ask to see them.

sections.h2: What to bring to the title agent
sections.html:
A first meeting goes faster with paper in hand. Bring a photo ID, the deed or the names of everyone on it, your latest tax bill, and permit numbers with final inspection dates for the roof, windows and air conditioning. If the house is vacant or inherited, add any court papers that show who may sign.

Mention open permits, an unpermitted shed or a pending dispute over value right away. Surprises found late in the process give a buyer a reason to lower the price or walk, while problems disclosed up front can be priced in and settled.

Once you accept an offer, the title agent searches the records for liens and mortgages, and anything found is paid out of your proceeds. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the date depends mostly on that search and on your permits.

  1. Sign the contract and settle who pays stamp tax, title insurance and recording.
  2. Close or disclose any open permit.
  3. Order payoff figures from lenders and the tax collector.
  4. Sign the deed; the clerk records it and collects the tax.

faqs.q: Does the City of St. Cloud need to approve a roof replacement?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists reroofing as work that requires a building permit. Hold on to the permit and final inspection records, because buyers and insurers often request them.

faqs.q: How long do I have to challenge my assessment?
faqs.a: File a petition with the clerk within 25 days after the August notice of proposed taxes. Appeals of a denied exemption have 30 days from the date the denial letter is mailed.

faqs.q: Can I paint or replace carpet without a permit in St. Cloud?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists painting, carpeting, cabinets and gutters among work that does not need a building permit. Confirm unusual projects with the building department.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead cap?
faqs.a: No. Ownership changes at the sale, so on the next January 1 the assessment goes back to just value. Your buyer applies for a new homestead exemption by March 1.

faqs.q: How can I pay St. Cloud permit fees?
faqs.a: Not in cash. The city does not accept cash at its counters, and staff can explain the other payment methods.
